All the stats are massively in Manchester City’s favour but the important statistic, the scoreline, remains level.

The first half is brought to an end and tempers are flaring as the two sides head off, with the game level at 0-0 at the break. The Porto fans and players are not happy with the officiating and Enzo is also involved in some antics.

Gvardiol needs to be careful as he is not punished for delaying a restart when you consider he is already on a booking. The Porto fans want to see a second yellow but the referee says the ball was moving so Porto could not take the restart.

Three added minutes to conclude this first half.

Should Guehi be in trouble here? He appears in real time to win his header but when you watch the replays he led with his arm. He catches Veiga right in the face and Guehi could be in some strife. However, VAR is not going to take any further action and Guehi can count himself lucky. The medics are on to tend to Veiga and you do wonder why VAR has not recommended a review. The ridiculous thing about that was that Guehi was not punished with a yellow card or even a free-kick. That clearly shows the referee did not properly see it.

Porto fans quick to remind Ruben Dias and Enzo Fernandez of their Benfica history. They jeered the pair when they got on the ball. Enzo is getting it from all angles at the moment, with Coventry fans taunting him at the weekend. He can expect more of that in the Premier League after his part in England’s exit at the World Cup, which led to Argentina players holding up a flag saying the Falkland Islands were Argentina’s.

Tensions are boiling over. They have been threatening to do so between Gomes and Gvardiol for a little while and now they do. Gomes steals the ball off Gvardiol and attempts to counter but is pulled back by Gvardiol, who is rightly booked. Gomes is not happy with Gvardiol and they come to blows.

D Costa twice denies Manchester City in a matter of seconds. First he saves from Haaland, then gets to his feet to deny Cherki. Manchester City are knocking on the door and you do feel like a goal is coming for Enzo Maresca’s side.

No goals in Porto but Real Madrid have their second at home against Inter Milan through Fede Valverde.

Manchester City struggled to carve out any genuine chances in the opening quarter of an hour but there are creating more and more opportunities, the latest falling to Foden, whose shot from the right side of the box looking for the far corner is saved by D Costa.

It is not often you see Haaland miss two good chances with his head in quick succession but that is what has happened. Semenyo cuts inside on the left onto his right and curls in a cross into a good area. He picks out Haaland but the Norwegian’s header misses the target. He knows he should have done better as he shakes his head in frustration.

Porto’s front three have struggled to have much of an impact in the game, in particular Silva up top, who has been almost non-existent.

A great save from D Costa to deny Haaland. Foden’s cross just before the byline on the left side of the box picks out Haaland. The Norwegian has barely touched the ball tonight but comes close to opening the scoring. However, D Costa is on hand to deny him with a fine save. Should Haaland have given D Costa the chance to save it? Maybe not.

Diogo Costa CLAWS away Erling Haaland's header 🧤Man City come closest so far in Porto 👀 pic.twitter.com/KVnBHdbNlH

In probably the marquee match-up of the night, Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid are taking on Inter Milan at the Bernabeu. Real have just taken the lead through Kylian Mbappe.

Semenyo cuts inside from the left and gets a shot away from the edge of the box but it is straight at D Costa. That was Manchester City’s first shot of the night.

Veiga has a shot saved at the near post by Donnarumma but the offside flag goes up. Veiga and Pep exchange a neat one-two down Porto’s left before Veiga’s effort is saved but Pepe was offside in the build-up.

Manchester City are dominating possession and perhaps it was a ploy by Enzo Marecsa to take it slowly and hog the ball in order to take the early sting out of Porto. The visitors would have been expecting the hosts would want to start hot so maybe they were willing to be slow on the ball in order to quieten down the crowd early doors. They have not had a shot yet and not really threatened the Porto goal but the hosts have not offered much going forward.

The weather in Porto really is horrible, the type of weather you would expect in Manchester in mid-November than Porto in early September.

Porto have a strong defensive record thus far this season but undoubtedly they will be tested a lot more tonight than they are in Liga Portugal. You would also imagine they will have to be clinical in attack as they are unlikely to create as many chances as they do domestically.

With it hammering down, Porto boss Francesco Farioli has swapped his lovely suit that he was wearing pre-game for a tracksuit top and cap. At half-time, he will probably head back in drenched like all the players if he is active in his dugout.

We are under way at the Estádio do Dragão with the rain still teaming down in Porto. Manchester City’s Champions League campaign gets going.

It has been pouring down in Porto but that has not dampened the spirits of the home fans, who are in fine voice ahead of kick-off. The pyrotechnics have gone off and it is loud inside the Dragão. Both sides then emerge from the tunnel and here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:

The horse named after his son defeated Najidi Storm, which was started the race with 1-33 odds. It means the favourite is now the shortest-priced loser in British racing history. Foden’s family also call him “Ronnie”, which is the name he gave his son.

Barcelona were unhappy with this after he took charge of a clash against Inter Milan which ended in an epic defeat.

Aston Villa have held on to beat Club Brugge 3-2 and you can catch all the reaction to that game right here.

The big news here at Estádio do Dragão is that Ayyoub Bouaddi is given his full Manchester City debut, after coming off the bench in previous Premier League games. The Morocco midfielder, 18, starts in midfield in place of Elliot Anderson from the team that defeated Coventry at the weekend. Phil Foden is also given the nod, replacing Iliman Ndiaye.

In the forward line for Porto tonight is Brazilian winger William Gomes. He was linked with a move to the Premier League over the summer and you would expect will continue to be on the radar of English clubs going forward.

It has been a positive start for Unai Emery’s Aston Villa out in Belgium as they lead Club Brugge 3-1 at half-time.

Enzo Maresca takes charge of his first Champions League game in charge of Manchester City as they have travelled to Portugal to take on Porto at the Estadio do Dragao. These sides last met during the Champions League group stages during the 2020/21 season. Manchester City won 3-1 at home before the two sides drew 0-0 in this stadium.

Manchester City were busy late on in the transfer window, bringing in both Iliman Ndiaye and Enzo Fernandez as they spent nearly £200m on deadline day alone. They come into tonight’s game off the back of three straight Premier League victories to kick off the Maresca era. Maresca has limited Champions League experience as a manager, which came with Chelsea last season. Manchester City have won their opening game of a Champions League campaign in six of the last seven seasons but this will be the first time since 2015/16 that Manchester City embark on a Champions League campaign without Pep Guardiola at the helm.

“It is a hard place to come [Porto],” said Maresca. “They have started really well. In the last 14/15 games in Europe they lost just one, that shows a difficult place to come, but we will try our best and try to win the game. It is a very, very good team. They have different players, but in terms of the team it is very clear in the way they play. They are aggressive without the ball and on the ball, they have a clear style. But we will try our best and try to win the game. The ambition is the same; try to be ourselves and to win games and then we will see.”

Porto, managed by Francesco Farioli, have won every league game so far this season and already sit four points clear at the summit of Liga Portugal. Farioli takes charge of his first game as a manger in the Champions League and the club make their return to the elite European competition after two seasons away.

“We are going to face one of the big favourites to win the competition,” Farioli said. “It will be a game that will demand that we be at our best, and we know that whenever we step onto the Dragão pitch, something special can happen. I am happy to be in the Champions League for the first time at 37 years old. This will be my first game, but we approach every game with the same attention to detail and the same focus. It is easy for the players to be motivated tomorrow [tonight]. But the key will be our strategy and our ability to execute it, individually and collectively.”

Porto were in the Europa League last season, making it to the quarter-finals, where they were knocked out by Nottingham Forest 2-1 on aggregate. The omens would not appear to be on Porto’s side tonight; they have only won two of their last 16 games against English opposition in major European competition.

Team news from Portugal to follow shortly.

#1828. Prediction: Crystal Palace vs Hoffenheim

Turning their attention back to Europa League action on Thursday evening, Crystal Palace will welcome Hoffenheim to Selhurst Park.

With Europe’s elite club competitions stealing all of the midweek attention, there are plenty of eye-catching betting promotions available.

With all eyes falling on south London, you can find all of the key Crystal Palace vs Hoffenheim H2H stats here.

Verdict: Crystal Palace win & Under 4.5 goals

Starting with the hosts, while Pierre Sage might have only arrived at Selhurst Park over the summer, the former Lens boss already finds the pressure on his shoulders at a boiling point. Although the Eagles might have extended on their EFL Cup adventure last week as they snatched a 1-0 victory away at Fulham, Crystal Palace came immediately crashing back down to earth. Last seen over the weekend getting hit with a 2-0 loss against Tottenham, Sage’s downbeat squad have dropped into the Premier League’s drop zone. Potentially facing a major battle in the race to keep hold of their top-flight status this year, Thursday’s hosts have mustered just a sole win from any of their previous six consecutive appearances across all competitions. With their worrying rut underlined by an infamous 5-0 drumming against arch-rivals Brighton on October 18th, Crystal Palace are desperately searching for an essential Europa League boost here.

While French international Jean-Philippe Mateta might have been shown an early Premier League red card away at Tottenham on Saturday, Palace’s leading marksman is free to feature here. However, sustaining a recent groin injury and once again missing out over the weekend, Sage’s side are once again expected to be without the services of Ismaila Sarr.

Making a timely return between the sticks over the past fortnight, club captain and England international Dean Henderson will start between the sticks. Despite coming under plenty of recent scrutiny, Chelsea loanee Axel Disasi should keep his spot at the heart of Palace’s defence.

As for the visitors, while Hoffenheim might have claimed their own respective essential boost last month, Christian Ilzer’s men have come crashing back down to earth. Last seen over the weekend putting in a toothless performance as they eventually fell to a 2-0 loss away at Werder Bremen, the Blues find themselves in a similar position to Thursday’s opponents. Despite shattering a string of records last season, Hoffenheim have drastically failed to replicate a similar level this time around. Crashing out of the DFP Pokal last week as they were hit with penalty shootout heartbreak against Kiel, Illzer’s side have also gained an unwanted reputation for their glaring struggles away from the SNP Arena. Getting their Europa League adventure underway with another 2-0 defeat against Greek outfit OFI Crete on September 17th, Hoffenheim have lost five of their previous six showdowns on the road.

Missing out against Werder Bremen over the weekend with a reported thigh issue, Hoffenheim are once again sweating over the fitness of former West Ham defender Vladimir Coufal. Likewise, all still recovering from respective injury blows, Ilzer’s side will travel to south London without the likes of Patrick Wimmer, Albian Hajdari and Nathan De Cat here.

Now in his fourth campaign at the SNP Arena, one-time Liverpool defender Ozan Kabak will start at the heart of Hoffenheim’s defence. Registering three direct goal contributions in as many Europa League appearances (one goal, two assists), veteran striker Andrej Kramaric will shoulder plenty of the Blues’ attacking threat.

With the pressure on Sage’s shoulders starting to reach a boiling point, Crystal Palace are desperately searching for a much-welcomed Europa League boost here. Currently sat in the drop zone among England’s elite, we could be set for a nail-biting showdown from Selhurst Park on Thursday night. Watching Hoffenheim lose five of their previous six showdowns away from the SNP Arena across all competitions, Palace will be eager to kickstart their campaign. Although we are backing a home victory in south London, it’s worth highlighting that the Eagles have registered just a sole strike in over 300 minutes of action.

Verdict: Crystal Palace win & Under 4.5 goals

#1827. Jose Mourinho addresses Trent Alexander-Arnold's Madrid future

By Naim Beneddra | 01 Nov 2026 09:02

Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho has addressed speculation surrounding Trent Alexander-Arnold's future, insisting that he does not expect the former Liverpool defender to seek a move away despite losing his place to Federico Valverde.

The England international has endured a frustrating spell at the Santiago Bernabeu, with Mourinho preferring to deploy the Uruguayan midfielder at right-back ahead of two specialists in Alexander-Arnold and Denzel Dumfries.

However, the Portuguese coach has now explained the reasoning behind that controversial decision, admitting that leaving both defenders on the bench has been uncomfortable.

Speaking ahead of Sunday's La Liga encounter with Racing Santander, Mourinho revealed that he had personally discussed the situation with Alexander-Arnold and Dumfries, both of whom had responded positively.

The 63-year-old also confirmed that Valverde would not start against Racing, offering one of the two defenders an opportunity to reclaim the position.

Alexander-Arnold's limited involvement has prompted questions about his long-term prospects in Madrid, with speculation linking the former Liverpool star with a possible return to the Premier League.

Mourinho's recent selection decisions have only intensified those concerns.

Despite having two established international right-backs available, the Real Madrid boss has preferred Valverde in the position during his side's recent resurgence, which includes five consecutive victories across all competitions.

However, Mourinho acknowledged that his tactical preference had created a difficult situation for the players affected.

"This pains me. I don't like creating bad feelings in my players; I like creating good ones," Mourinho explained during Saturday's press conference, as quoted by Real Madrid's official website.

"When you build a squad based on two players per position and then make a third play, it's something I don't like, that hurts me, and that makes me sad."

The former Chelsea and Manchester United manager nevertheless insisted that his decision had been based entirely on the team's tactical requirements.

"I thought that at that particular moment, the best thing for the team was to change the midfield and play Fede as a much more offensive full-back than the others, thinking about the team and less about the players."

Valverde's repositioning has allowed Mourinho to experiment with different midfield combinations, including the use of Arda Guler and Bernardo Silva alongside Aurelien Tchouameni.

The adjustment has coincided with Madrid's improved performances, most notably their 2-1 victory over Barcelona in last weekend's El Clasico.

Mourinho revealed that he had explained his reasoning directly to the two players whose opportunities had been restricted.

"I have had good acceptance from Trent and Dumfries when we explained to them that it was a decision for the team and not against the players."

Asked about the possibility of either defender seeking an exit, Mourinho added: "I don't think they will be asking for any kind of exit."

His comments provide a response to the uncertainty surrounding Alexander-Arnold, whose reduced involvement has already fuelled speculation about a potential departure.

However, Mourinho's confidence that the England international will remain at the club should not be mistaken for a guarantee over his future or an assurance that he will return to the starting lineup permanently.

The immediate situation has changed ahead of Madrid's trip to Racing Santander, with Valverde omitted from the travelling squad after experiencing muscular discomfort following El Clasico.

Mourinho had initially announced that the 28-year-old would not start Sunday's match, but Madrid subsequently confirmed their squad without the Uruguayan.

That development leaves Alexander-Arnold and Dumfries competing for the right-back position, although the manager has not revealed which player will receive the nod.

The circumstances are particularly significant for Alexander-Arnold, who has struggled to establish himself as Mourinho's preferred option since the Portuguese coach took charge.

The decision to start Valverde against Barcelona had raised fresh doubts about the futures of both recognised right-backs.

Alexander-Arnold and Dumfries were eventually introduced during that victory, but their involvement did little to settle questions about the longer-term hierarchy.

Mourinho has now sought to reassure his defenders that opportunities will come as Madrid navigate a demanding schedule.

"In the end, everyone will play," he insisted.

The Spanish giants face Racing on Sunday before travelling to Greece for a Champions League encounter with AEK Athens on Wednesday, followed by another away fixture against Valencia next Saturday.

Mourinho pointed to the accumulation of matches, fatigue, suspensions and potential injuries as reasons why he will need to rotate his squad.

For Alexander-Arnold, Sunday's match could therefore represent an important opportunity to demonstrate that he can meet the tactical demands which have led Mourinho to favour Valverde.

His manager has attempted to dismiss concerns about a possible departure, but the battle for regular playing time remains unresolved.

#1825. Liverpool vs. Arsenal: Why Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyokeres must not start together - "Will never work"

By Ben Knapton | 01 Nov 2026 09:37

Ahead of Sunday's Liverpool vs. Arsenal Premier League blockbuster, Sports Mole site coordinator Ben Knapton discusses the Gunners' chances of responding to their shock EFL Cup loss to Fleetwood Town and urges Mikel Arteta to end a starting XI experiment that has "never worked".

Embarrassing, humiliating, catastrophic. There aren't enough superlatives to describe [the Fleetwood loss]. From the way we were playing in those first 70 minutes, maybe I was expecting it.

Certainly wasn't expecting it two days before the game when I did the preview and backed us to win 4-0. 4-0 was a scoreline a lot of people would have expected, especially with the team Arteta put out.

I knew he was going to make lots of changes, but in hindsight I thought even a much-changed Arsenal team would still get the job done.

There's been so much talk this season about Arsenal's squad depth, about how they have two players for each position, a second team if you like.

If that second team can't beat a team that's 83 places below you in the English football pyramid, you can't really talk up Arsenal's squad depth.

Maybe there was some arrogance in there. Maybe they went in expecting an easier night than they got. But some players just showed they are not first-team quality.

I don't want to attack the young players too much, but Marli Salmon was not strong enough at all for Fleetwood's goal. He was shrugged off far, far too easily.

Havertz and Gyokeres starting together does not work. That does not work, that has never worked. The EFL Cup final in March when Havertz and Gyokeres started together in that game.

It did not work at all then, it did not work at Fleetwood. Kai Havertz was maybe one of the worst players on the pitch, missed a couple of chances, had no creative influence in that number 10 role.

If they're going to start together, start them as a front two in a complete emergency, which to be fair we're not far away from with all the injuries and now Dowman's three-game suspension.

Stick Kai Havertz on the right wing, he can play there, he has played there. When Arsenal do their combinations on the right-hand side, Havertz does sometimes drift over to that right flank.

But starting Havertz behind Gyokeres doesn't work, will never work.

So for this Liverpool game, Dowman is out, Bukayo Saka is out. Tzolis may be back, but I would be surprised if he starts.

Madueke also missed that game against Fleetwood with an ankle injury, so could potentially be four wide options out, but I think Madueke will be fine for this one.

I'd be very surprised if Declan Rice doesn't start this one either, and I'm expecting a big, big response.

He's going to revert to type in terms of the starting 11, drop the likes of Zubimendi, bring back in Declan Rice. He's got a big decision to make up top after Havertz and Gyokeres have both really, really struggled.

Even though Arteta was being quite measured in his post-game assessment to the media, he was fuming internally. The players would have absolutely got the hairdryer treatment in the dressing room.

I think there will be a massive, massive response at Liverpool.

#1824. Barcelona vs Aston Villa - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Knapton | 01 Nov 2026 10:28, Last updated: 01 Nov 2026 11:01

Unai Emery returns to the location of La Remontada on Tuesday evening, when Champions League perfectionists Aston Villa face a fierce test of their continental mettle against Barcelona at Camp Nou.

The Lions arrive in Catalonia with an unblemished record of three wins from three in the 2026-27 tournament, while their hosts' unbeaten start came to an end at the home of holders Paris Saint-Germain on matchday three.

The champions and the challengers colliding at the Parc des Princes promised to serve up a glut of goals, and in true PSG vs. Barcelona fashion, the two beleaguered backlines failed to quell the two absorbing attacks during the 90 minutes.

Unfortunately for the La Liga champions, four of the six strikes scored on the evening went PSG's way, as a Blaugrana side who began the season with 11 straight victories in all competitions lost their 100% record in crushing fashion.

Barca's first defeat of the campaign soon became a mini-wobble, as Jose Mourinho inspired Real Madrid to an unexpected Camp Nou Clasico triumph in La Liga, but Flick's men returned to their merciless ways on Saturday evening.

Indeed, the Blaugrana snapped their two-game losing sequence in a 6-1 annihilation of Alaves, thus maintaining a two-point advantage over nearest rivals Atletico Madrid at the top of the La Liga table.

Only once this season have Barcelona failed to score more than two goals in one game - their 1-2 reverse to Real Madrid just last month - although Alaves' consolation on Saturday means that Flick's side are also without a clean sheet in five.

In fact, Barca have shipped at least one goal in nine of their last 10 games in all competitions, but they are unbeaten in 15 straight UEFA home games against English teams, last suffering defeat to Liverpool almost two decades ago.

PSG's beating of Barcelona on matchday three means that the reigning European champions are the only team to out-perform Aston Villa in the 2026-27 league phase, as Emery's men sit in a scarcely believable second position after three rounds.

Club Brugge, Fenerbahce and Viking FK have all fallen to Villa's might thus far, the latter failing to follow up their extraordinary draw with Bayern Munich as Emery masterminded a comfortable 3-1 triumph in the West Midlands on October 21.

As well as being just one of five teams on a perfect nine points, Villa's 12 UCL goals scored is the joint second-best record behind PSG's 14, while +9 goal difference is also the best of its kind alongside the two-time winners.

A 2-1 success over Manchester City just three days after the Viking win enhanced Emery's reputation as one of the globe's finest head coaches at this moment in time, but his side now travel to Camp Nou on a two-game winless run, following up a 3-0 EFL Cup loss at Bournemouth with a disappointing 1-1 Premier League draw at home to Fulham.

Aston Villa have also prevailed in just one of their four historical meetings with Barcelona, although not since the 1983 UEFA Super Cup final - which the Lions won 3-1 on aggregate over two legs - have the Lions and the Blaugrana squared off in a competitive setting.

The injury that forced Dani Olmo off in the first half of Barca's loss to PSG is a moderately severe one, as the Spanish playmaker is expected to remain out until after the next international break with a torn adductor muscle.

Olmo is joined on the sidelines by Xavi Espart (ankle), Andreas Christensen (thigh), Roony Bardghji (ACL), Eric Garcia (thigh) and Jules Kounde (ankle), but the hosts suffered no new concerns against Alaves over the weekend.

Scorer of two goals and provider of one on Saturday, Lamine Yamal has another record in his sights; if he finds the net on Tuesday, he will break the record for the most Champions League goals as a teenager, currently sitting level with Kylian Mbappe on 13.

As for Aston Villa, it is as you were on the team news front, and Emery should only be missing Amadou Onana (knee), Matteo Ruggeri (thigh) and Aaron Wan-Bissaka (thigh) for the trip to Catalonia.

Some concerns were raised over Nicolas Jackson's availability when the striker was not pictured in training last week, but he was fit enough to start and score against Fulham, moving onto eight strikes from his first 12 games in a Villa kit.

Leon Goretzka - a member of the Bayern Munich team that destroyed Barca 8-2 in 2020 - made his first Premier League start against Fulham too, but Joao Gomes may be preferred on Tuesday if Emery errs on the side of caution with the German.

J. Garcia; Cancelo, Martin, Cubarsi, Balde; Pedri, Rodri; Yamal, Lopez, Gordon; Raphinha

Suzuki; Cash, Lindelof, Torres, Maatsen; Kamara, Gomes; McGinn, Manzambi, Buendia; Jackson

Goals at both ends are normally a guarantee when Barcelona are involved, and fans should expect no different when two teams with 23 Champions League goals between them collide at Camp Nou.

However, Villa have also conceded at least twice in three of their last five away matches, and Emery's men may be overwhelmed by Flick's ferocious attack as their 100% UCL record comes to an end.

#1821. Chaotic scenes at London Palladium's glitzy Ballon d'Or ceremony as huge crowds of fans try to gain access to red carpet event to catch a glimpse of Harry Kane and Co - and a photographer gets into a spat with security!

Published: 17:34 EDT, 26 October 2026 | Updated: 05:33 EDT, 29 October 2026

Police were forced to push back large crowds attempting to access the Ballon d'Or red carpet as the start of the marquee football awards ceremony was delayed in London.

The ceremony had been due to start at 8pm at the London Palladium, but organisers were forced into a half-an-hour delay.

The delay came with Ballon d'Or contenders Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappe among those having just arrived at the event, amid chaotic scenes nearby.

Footage shared on social media revealed that large crowds had gathered by the venue in Oxford Street in an attempt to catch a glimpse of leading sporting and showbiz names attending the ceremony.

One clip showed police near the red carpet having to hold back fans, who appeared to be trying to push through barriers to gain access to the event sparking security fears.

Daily Mail Sport has contacted organisers for comment.

Footage shared on social media showed crowds being forced back by security as they attempted to gain access to the Ballon d'Or red carpet at the London Palladium (Source: TikTok: @winstonso7)

Fans had been hoping to get a glimpse of stars including England captain Harry Kane on the red carpet

Real Madrid and France star Kylian Mbappe was another star in attendance as he hoped to claim the Ballon d'Or for the first time

A photographer was seen clashing with a security guard on the event's official broadcast after he was pulled back on the red carpet. (Source: DAZN)

The awards ceremony – overseen by France Football – has been taking place in London for the first time in its 70-year history, with all previous editions having been held in France.

The decision to stage the event in London was made to honour Sir Stanley Matthews, who won the first Ballon d'Or back in 1956.

The security concerns outside the venue came as part of a chaotic build-up to the ceremony, which included a clash between a photographer and a security guard on the official broadcast.

The photographer appeared to inadvertently walk into DAZN's red carpet broadcast, with the security guard seen trying to pull him away.

After the security guard intervened to move him away again, the photographer could be heard saying 'stop grabbing me.'

Ballon d'Or organisers had endured embarrassment in the build-up to the event after three articles were posted on their official website which each announced Kane, Lamine Yamal and Mbappe as the winner of this year's men's prize.

Organisers, who were alerted by Daily Mail Sport, subsequently removed the articles and launched an investigation.

#1817. Chelsea could sell £70m Fofana and Malo Gusto in 2027

By Naim Beneddra | 01 Nov 2026 10:46

Chelsea are reportedly considering making two high-profile defenders available for transfer in 2027, with doubts growing over their ability to meet Xabi Alonso's long-term requirements.

The Blues could be prepared to part ways with Wesley Fofana, who joined from Leicester City for approximately £70m in 2022, while fellow French international Malo Gusto is also facing an uncertain future at Stamford Bridge.

According to Flashscore journalist Dean Jones, Chelsea's hierarchy are becoming increasingly concerned about the reliability of their defensive options and are assessing potential changes to the squad ahead of next year's transfer windows.

Both players came under scrutiny following Wednesday's EFL Cup elimination against Liverpool, when Fofana missed the decisive penalty in a 6-5 shootout defeat after a 1-1 draw.

However, the concerns reportedly extend beyond that result, with Chelsea evaluating whether the pair can provide the consistency required to compete at the highest level.

Fofana's position has become particularly uncertain despite the substantial investment Chelsea made to secure his signature four years ago.

The former Leicester defender arrived at Stamford Bridge as one of the most expensive centre-backs in Premier League history, but recurring injuries have prevented him from establishing himself as a consistently available first-team player.

His lengthy absences have disrupted his development and made it difficult for Chelsea to build a settled defensive partnership around him.

According to Jones, the Blues are now assessing whether Fofana can fulfil the role originally envisaged for him, with the 25-year-old at risk of losing his place in the club's plans during 2027.

The Frenchman's performance against Liverpool reportedly reinforced existing concerns, particularly after he missed the penalty that ended Chelsea's involvement in the competition.

Nevertheless, his recent involvement under Alonso offers a more complicated picture.

Having gone without an appearance for much of October, Fofana returned to the starting lineup at Anfield before retaining his place against Manchester United on Saturday.

Although he struggled during a first half in which United created several promising opportunities, the defender subsequently played an important role in Chelsea's 2-0 victory.

Lisandro Martinez was dismissed after catching Fofana with his arm inside the penalty area, allowing Cole Palmer to convert the resulting spot kick and double Chelsea's lead.

His involvement in that decisive incident underlined that he remains part of Alonso's immediate plans, even as questions persist over his longer-term future.

Fofana is contracted to Chelsea until June 2029, meaning any prospective departure would require an agreement between the club, the player and an interested suitor.

His injury record and substantial original transfer fee could also complicate Chelsea's attempts to secure a satisfactory deal.

Fofana is not the only French defender whose position has come under review.

Gusto, who joined Chelsea from Lyon in January 2023, is reportedly another player the club could consider moving on as part of a wider defensive overhaul.

The Blues have already begun exploring potential replacements at right-back, according to an earlier Flashscore report, with scouts assessing options across Europe.

The 23-year-old remains under contract until 2030, but his reduced involvement this season has raised questions about his place in Alonso's preferred system.

Marco Palestra has emerged as a competing option on the right, making Gusto's prospects of securing consistent playing time increasingly uncertain.

Chelsea reportedly valued the former Lyon defender at around €80m during the summer, although that figure is now being reassessed.

Interest has previously been attributed to Manchester City, Paris Saint-Germain, Bayern Munich, Atletico Madrid, Liverpool and Tottenham Hotspur, but there is no indication that Chelsea have received a formal offer.

Gusto was introduced as a late substitute against Manchester United, highlighting his continued involvement despite speculation surrounding his future.

The possibility of losing both French defenders would represent a significant change in Chelsea's squad planning, particularly given their ages and the long-term contracts awarded to them.

However, no final decision has been announced, and Flashscore's reporting does not establish that either player will necessarily leave during the January window.

Chelsea's willingness to consider offers may ultimately depend on the availability of suitable replacements and whether interested clubs can meet their financial expectations.

#1816. Ivan Toney's trial over assault at exclusive London nightclub will start in 20 MONTHS - putting England star's Euro 2028 prospects at risk

Published: 06:44 EDT, 29 October 2026 | Updated: 07:06 EDT, 29 October 2026

The assault trial of England international Ivan Toney will not be heard for another 20 months – potentially ruling him out of Euro 2028.

The trial will begin on June 12, 2028 - three days into the European Championships, which will take placed in the UK and Ireland - and is expected to last three to four days.

Toney, who was in this summer's World Cup squad, appeared at Southwark Crown Court for a pre-trial hearing on Thursday morning and pleaded not guilty to assault occasioning actual bodily harm.

The 30-year-old is accused of headbutting and punching Saber Da Silva at the 100 Wardour Street nightclub in Soho on December 6 2025.

Toney’s defence do not dispute that he caused the injury but claim he acted in self-defence.

Judge Christopher Hehir labelled the case ‘straightforward’ and apologised for the long wait until the trial. He cited the significant backlog in the judicial system, before warning Toney that it is a criminal offence not to turn up for the case.

Toney arrived at court at 9.10am on Thursday, flanked by a six-man entourage, wearing a black button-up cardigan with a white shirt, black tie and grey trousers. He will remain on bail until his trial.

Ivan Toney arrives at Southwark Crown Court for his hearing on Thursday morning

Toney was charged on July 31 after a Metropolitan Police investigation. When the charge was announced, a spokesperson for Toney said: ‘Ivan acknowledges the charge and although he is naturally shocked, he looks forward to being given the opportunity to clear his name in court.’

The England striker initially appeared at Westminster Magistrates' Court last month, where he opted to have his case heard by a jury at the Crown Court.

In October, the court heard that Toney and Da Silva ‘squared up’ before the striker ‘lunged forward and head-butted the complainant, followed by a few punches’.

The 30-year-old is currently plying his trade in Saudi Arabia for Al-Ahli and has scored 13 goals in 14 appearances this season. He left England for £40million in 2024, having scored 36 Premier League goals in 83 appearances for Brentford.

Toney started for England in their 6-4 World Cup bronze medal match against France but was left out of the most recent Three Lions squad.

#1815. Aston Villa predicted lineup vs. Barcelona: Leon Goretzka dropped in double change

By Ben Knapton | 01 Nov 2026 10:57

Aston Villa boss Unai Emery could make two changes to his starting lineup for Tuesday's Champions League battle with Barcelona at Camp Nou.

The Lions are searching for a fourth win from four European contests this season, having already got the better of Club Brugge, Fenerbahce and Viking FK while netting 12 goals along the way.

Emery will still be missing Amadou Onana (knee), Matteo Ruggeri (thigh) and Aaron Wan-Bissaka (thigh) for Tuesday's glamour tie, but Villa are otherwise in good nick for matchday four.

Nicolas Jackson was not spotted in training photos before Saturday's 1-1 Premier League draw with Fulham, but the Senegal international started and scored against the Cottagers to take his total to eight goals from 12 games in a Villa kit.

Jackson will undoubtedly lead the line at Camp Nou, likely with John McGinn and Johan Manzambi in support, but Emery may choose to lean on the experience of Emiliano Buendia as Alysson makes way.

Leon Goretzka, who was part of the Bayern Munich team that demolished Barcelona 8-2 in 2020, made his full Premier League debut on Saturday, but the German could also make way for Joao Gomes as Emery plays it safe with his fitness.

Rejuvenated in a claret kit, Victor Lindelof will once again join forces with Pau Torres, who lost seven of his eight meetings with Barcelona during his time at Villarreal from 2016 to 2023.

Zion Suzuki's own-goal blunder gifted Fulham a point at Villa Park, but there is no chance of the Japan international making way in Catalonia.

Suzuki; Cash, Lindelof, Torres, Maatsen; Kamara, Gomes; McGinn, Manzambi, Buendia; Jackson

#1814. Mac Allister not so sad now after Liverpool comeback winner

Do your talking on the pitch, as the old adage goes, and Alexis Mac Allister emphatically did just that as Liverpool came from behind to thrillingly win their first Champions League tie under new head coach Andoni Iraola in what was his debut at this level.

On the eve of this encounter, against a strong Atlético Madrid, one of the clubs who have recently tried to sign him, Mac Allister had spoken of his sadness. Sadness that, unlike fellow midfielders Dominik Szoboszlai – Liverpool’s other scorer here – and Ryan Gravenberch, he had not been offered and signed a new contract.

So, earn it. And many more goals – and overall performances like this – there is no doubt the Argentinian will have a deal placed in front of him. He scored with an arresting second-half shot, which proved to be the winner, and the smile across his face said it all. Not so sad now as he was later substituted to a standing ovation with Gravenberch taking his place.

The goal came early in the second half, with Iraola attributing that to adjusting his tactics after being flummoxed by Atlético’s back five and packed midfield in a first half when Liverpool were second best.

Mac Allister was heavily involved through the build-up, eventually picking out Rio Ngumoha on the left whose shot was blocked and pinballed around. It dropped to Mac Allister, 20 yards out, and he hit the kind of unerring drive that gives the goalkeeper no chance. And so it proved. Boom. And Anfield was bouncing.

Mac Allister FIRES Liverpool into the lead at Anfield! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/KGOvuAEU4W

There are certainly signs under Iraola, and following a difficult last campaign, that Mac Allister is beginning to rediscover the form he showed during his first two seasons at Liverpool. Time and again the 27-year-old made vital interventions, showed aggression and walked the tightrope of a harsh early yellow card. He dovetailed with Szoboszlai and that might be a concern for Gravenberch – watched by the Netherlands’ new head coach Xavi Hernández – if Iraola persists with this approach.

Although Mac Allister has two years left on his current deal, the last thing Liverpool need is yet another attention-sapping contract saga, even if he is not the same scale of player as Mohamed Salah or Trent Alexander-Arnold.

For Iraola, after three Premier League games, comprising two draws and a victory over newly-promoted Ipswich Town, this will hopefully be lift off. A big European night at Anfield and coming from behind to beat one of the continent’s heavyweights.

“I loved it,” Iraola said, before castigating himself for misreading the way Atlético would line up. And what of Mac Allister’s riposte? There was a smile from Iraola before the Spaniard’s usual diplomacy kicked in as he talked about a “lovely, lovely goal” and how good it was for his midfielders to contribute.

Liverpool had to fight for it and what will have satisfied Iraola is that the defence, which has come under such scrutiny, held out. Even so, there are still serious concerns over the suitability of Milos Kerkez at left-back – who was badly at fault for Atlético’s goal – although the robust Ronald Araújo showed he can be a strong and versatile option on the other flank. The Uruguayan, signed on loan from Barcelona, is such a presence in both penalty areas and has the capacity to gain cult status.

As does £123m signing from Paris St-Germain Bradley Barcola, who should have scored – once, certainly, possibly twice – and possesses astonishing pace that will undoubtedly lead to goals. There are also encouraging signs that his presence could enliven Florian Wirtz. Barcola eventually also went off, but thankfully it was only to cramp.

There was a collective intake of breath across the Kop when Marcos Llorente was played through and bore down on them to give Atlético the lead. There was a desperate hope that he had strayed offside. There was then a realisation that Kerkez had, however, played him on with an appalling lack of awareness. Llorente beat Alisson.

It owed much to a wonderful shimmy, deceiving Szoboszlai in centre field, by Julián Alvarez before he smartly threaded the ball through, and Mac Allister’s international team-mate almost doubled Atlético’s advantage soon after. Only to be denied by Alisson.

Llorente breaks the deadlock! 🔥That's now FIVE Champions League goals for the Atletico man against Liverpool at Anfield 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Rxp4zurfpc

We knew, we feared it would be Llorente who scored. Remarkably, he has now half of his 10 goals in this competition against Liverpool. Indeed, he named his dog Anfield after his extra-time brace knocked Liverpool, then the holders, out in the last 16 in 2020. And Liverpool had made a dog’s dinner of defending this time.

This is a different Atlético. A far less defensive, far more expansive Atlético. In years gone by, once they were 1-0 it was game over under Diego Simeone. But these days they try and play more and that gives their opponents a chance. And so it proved.

Atlético goalkeeper Jan Oblak did well to deny Barcola, with his trailing foot, before Wirtz won the ball back and found Szoboszlai who eventually ended the movement. It owed much, however, to a clever backheel to pick out the midfielder who finished low into the corner. Who executed that backheel? That would be Araújo.

Szoboszlai slots home after a brilliant flick from Araujo! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UrHQTwtgsY

Barcola should have scored, sent clear by Wirtz in a brilliant, sweeping counter-attack, before Mac Allister did.

The question now was whether Liverpool would show the resilience to see through the result. As Iraola made changes, they answered that with a resounding yes, which will have pleased him as much as the result, as much as the comeback, as much as Mac Allister’s stunning response.

“I was enjoying it [the Anfield crowd]. They [Atletico Madrid] are a very good team. Technically, in the middle, lovely players. It is not easy to press those players as they have quality. They have been playing together forever. We find another comeback after Nottingham Forest, after Newcastle. We still have this thing to improve in the beginning of the games, but I am happy as we have shown some character. This is the Champions League, you do not have easy games.”

"You can see he's football mad." ⚽Steven Gerrard on Andoni Iraola's passion and the impact he's making at Liverpool 👏🎙️ @laura_woodsy | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/M3qKhxt8HE

There is the final whistle at Anfield and Liverpool start their Champions League campaign with a 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid. Liverpool did fall behind to Marcos Llorente’s goal but goals from Dominik Szoboszlai and Alexis Mac Allister give Andoni Iraola a win in his first Champions League game as a manager.

Victory in MD1 🤩 #UCL pic.twitter.com/SWFFhSudFJ

First Champions League game. First Champions League win for Andoni Iraola ✅ pic.twitter.com/D3CE6w6V0b

Koumas is tripped by Le Normand and that should be it.

That is a silly foul from Lookman, with Frimpong inside his own box running back towards his own goal, but Lookman decides to push him in the back.

Liverpool think they have sealed it through Frimpong but the offside flag has gone up. First Munoz cuts onto his right and has a shot saved by Oblak. The ball falls to Frimpong, who slots home but he was clearly offside when Munoz took the initial shot.

Kerkez is currently down with cramp and his night is done. He will be replaced by Tsimikas and Liverpool will make their final change at the same time. Koumas comes on for Isak.

Atletico win a corner but it all stems from sloppy play in the centre of the pitch from Gravenberch. He has had a few sloppy moments since coming on.

The corner is flicked on by Hjulmand but ends up coming to nothing.

It isn’t the headline making performance, by any means, but that shouldn’t dilute the importance of Ronald Araujo’s contribution for Liverpool tonight and, indeed, against Ipswich last Friday. He’s doing what Liverpool wanted him to, providing versatility and leadership in their back four and - more than anything - quality. He hasn’t put a foot wrong.

Atletico win a corner out on the left in front of their travelling supporters. Grimaldo’s outswinger is flicked on by the head of Hancko at the near post but it goes over.

Isak has the chance to potentially seal the victory for Liverpool but Le Normand makes a crucial block. Le Normand has only just come on but already made a couple of defensive actions.

Liverpool win a corner out on the left with the last touch coming off Pubill, who was marking Van Dijk from a free-kick. Szoboszlai’s inswinger is headed away by Le Normand.

Digeo Simeone is making his final two substitutions of the night as Le Normand and Hjulmad replace Romero and Barrios,

Atletico bring on David, on loan from Juventus, for Baena.

Alvarez has a chance inside the Liverpool box but his shot is straight at Alisson. There are some appeals for handball but it hit Munoz from such close range that it is never a penalty.

Liverpool are making a substitution as Mac Allister, who scored the goal to put Liverpool in front, is replaced by Gravenberch. Mac Allister, who made some comments in the press conference yesterday about his sadness at not being offered a new contract, put in a good performance in the centre of Liverpool’s midfield. He was on a booking though so probably sensible to take him off when you can guarantee that the Atletico players would have tried to get him sent off.

We’ll see what happens in the coming weeks and months but there have been glimmers here with Florian Wirtz looking better than he has done with pace to pass to; if it clicks with him, Bradley Barcola & Alexander Isak it could be exciting but one game must be built on. It’s frustrating that Barcola’s night has ended with what appears to be cramp or tightness in his calf because he was getting more joy than he had done before half-time. The big challenge for Liverpool, too, is whether they have the nous to see this contest out.

The new Netherlands boss Xavi is in attendance at Anfield tonight, watching the likes of Van Dijk, Frimpong and Gravenberch, although the latter is still yet to come off the Liverpool bench.

This is a concern for Liverpool. Barcola has gone down and seems to have some pain in his left calf. Is it cramp or an injury? It will be a double change for the home side as Frimpong and Munoz come on. Barcola is given a standing ovation as he goes off and the Liverpool fans will be hoping it is just cramp. Ngumoha also heads off.

Diego Simeone is going to make his first two changes of the night. Grimaldo and Lookman come on

It is all Liverpool as they sense a third goal is there for the taking. Ngumoha does well down Liverpool’s left and pushes it past Pubill, who slides in and takes him down. Pubill is booked. He cannot believe it but I do not know why; a clear foul and yellow card.

That is a stunning strike from the Argentine. The ball falls to the midfielder just outside the box and he hits it first time. He hits the ball so crisply and there is nothing Oblak can do to stop it. Liverpool should have taken the lead through Barcola moments before they do now have the lead for the first time tonight.

Mac Allister FIRES Liverpool into the lead at Anfield! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/KGOvuAEU4W

Well, that’s one way to prove you might warrant a new contract. A quite beautiful left footed drive from Alexis Mac Allister gives Liverpool the lead and it has been noticeable thus far in Andoni Iraola’s matches that his team get stronger at the start of the second period. Diego Simeone most wonder how Atleti are losing a game they were controlling but Liverpool’s speed on the break is proving very good at causing chaos.

Barcola should have his first Liverpool goal and the hosts should be ahead but the Frenchman misses the target. It is the perfect counter-attack really from Liverpool and it is Wirtz and Barcola who exchange passes from deep inside their own half all the way to the Atletico penalty area. Barcola drives forward, into the Atletico box, and you think he is going to slot it into the bottom corner but his effort goes just wide. Barcola could and perhaps should have a brace tonight.

Barcola wins the first corner of this second half off Hancko right in front of The Kop. Liverpol take it short before Mac Allister clips the ball in. Araujo meets it and his header is powerful but it is off target.

We are back under way at Anfield. No changes from either side at the break.

Some of the statistics are pretty even but Atletico Madrid have had just three touches in the Liverpool penalty area, yet have a goal to their name.

The first half at Anfield is brought to an end and it is level at 1-1 at the break. Llorente gave Atletico the lead before Szoboszlai equalised for Liverpool. The home fans let the officials know what they think of their performance in that first half.

One added minute at the end of this first half.

There has been about five minutes of squabbling between the Liverpool and Atletico benches, so much so that Tommy Elphick - Andoni Iraola’s assistant - missed Dominik Szoboszlai score the equaliser. Tensions have only increased after a nasty little challenge from Cristian Romero on Alexander Isak. The half-time whistle might be coming at a good time to defuse the situation but you fancy the walk back to the dressing rooms will be spicy.

The conduct of the Atletico players is frankly embarrassing, not a massive surprise from a Diego Simeone side. Kang goes down clutching his face when there was barely any contact and then, unlike Isak, he does not have to spend a minute off the pitch.

Isak is on the ground, clutching at his knee, after a heavy challenge from Romero. It is a nasty challenge from Romero, who remarkably is neither booked nor penalised. To compound the awful officiating, Isak now has to spend a minute off the pitch owing to the new rules. What do you make of that new rule of the player who is down going off for a minute? Have your say in the comments section at the bottom of the blog.

Moments after Liverpool equalised, Atletico have a decent opportunity to restore their lead but Baena drags his effort wide from the edge of the box.

Moments after Barcola could not take a big chance to equalise for Liverpool, Szoboslzai does. First, Barcola is denied by Oblak. Liverpool keep it alive inside the Atletico box and a simple sensational flick by Aruajo finds Szoboszlai, who finds the bottom corner with a clinical finish. Kerkez has been poor tonight but he deserves credit for his part in that goal as he was the player to initially win it back for Liverpool with a good press.

Szoboszlai slots home after a brilliant flick from Araujo! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UrHQTwtgsY

Liverpool look like a team that has been out of the Champions League for a couple of years and are only just finding its feet, which seems strange given they missed only one year in the last 10. They have glimmers of promise but they aren’t convincing anyone they will blow Atleti’s house down. One day everything will align for Atleti and they will reach another final. They have an outside chance this year, especially if Julian Alvarez - easily the best player on this pitch - has anything to do with it. Diego Simeone always has class strikers at the top of his team and Alvarez stands comparison with any who have gone before.

Wirtz has a great chance to equalise for Liverpool but his shot on the half volley is saved by Oblak. It would not have mattered anyway had the ball ended up in the net because Isak was offside before crossing for Wirtz.

Some of the officiating tonight has been appalling and the latest example is VAR taking a check on a possible red card for Mac Allister for a foul that is never a red card in a million years. The officials then take an age to give yet another obvious offside and, in the end, the referee gives it rather than the linesman. That really does sum up the officials tonight as the referee should not be the one to give offsides.

Alvarez shoots from distance and forces Alisson into a good save diving to his right. There was a suspicion of offside from Simeone in the build-up.

Atletico take it short but Simeone’s shot is blocked by Araujo.

What a save from Alisson! 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PuajED3Rks

The Anfield faithful are furious. Two fouls in quick succession are not given when they were both clearly fouls. The referee appears to have a different interpretation of body checks and taking people out off the ball than the rest of us.

The Spanish side take the lead at Anfield and it is another goal on this ground for Llorente. Alvarez feeds a through ball to pick out the run of Llorente, who is onside. He takes one touch before firing past Alisson from the edge of the box. That is poor, poor defending from Kerkez, who not only played Llorente onside but then did not track the run properly. Llorente now has five goals on this ground.

Llorente breaks the deadlock! 🔥That's now FIVE Champions League goals for the Atletico man against Liverpool at Anfield 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Rxp4zurfpc

The idea that Atletico Madrid are focused on spoiling and nullifying belongs in the past. They are an attractive team, well organised and you suspect they have the gears to cause Liverpool problems... and as we type, they have just opened the scoring by playing straight through Liverpool’s middle. It was a bad goal for home side to concede. Milos Kerkez was out of sync with the rest of Liverpool’s defence and Marcos Llorente has galloped straight through. As we said at the start: it’s a big test for the hosts... it’s just got even bigger.

A little line about Llorente, who has now scored five times against Liverpool in the Champions League. He is fond of playing in this arena, he named his dog “Anfield! when he bought it in 2021.

Chance for Barcola. Szoboszlai clips a lovely ball in behind down the right channel to pick out the run of Barcola. The Frenchman takes it down beautifully before having his shot saved by Oblak. Barcola’s best moment thus far tonight.

Baena takes a first-time effort on from a central position around 25 yards out but he cannot keep his effort down and it sails into The Kop.

Atletico were renowned for years under Diego Simeone is being very tight at the back and in midfield, especially away from home. However, in recent years they have become more expansive and as a result are more open.

Liverpool win their first corner of the night at the Anfield Road End in front of the travelling Atletico fans. They take it short and Szoboslzai takes it towards the Atletico box. It appeared to be a very obvious foul on Szoboszlai right on the edge of the box but nothing is given. At the very least, it should have been given a free-kick as there was definitely at least one foul.

Barcola, who has won the Champions League with PSG in the last two seasons, is starting out on the right for Liverpool tonight with Ngumoha on the left.

Big test for Liverpool and it will be fascinating to see how this formation works out. It looks very much like it is 4-4-2, with Florian Wirtz almost alongside Alexander Isak and Rio Ngumoha the left winger and Bradley Barcola on the opposite flank - a position Andoni Iraola has referenced him playing in Lyon as a teenager. It’s also a big test for Iraola against Diego Simeone, the wily and vastly experienced manager, who is immaculately dressed - as always - in his trademark black suit.

Liverpool have a chance inside the opening minute. Szoboszlai wins it inside his own half and drives forward. He then plays it out to his right to find Isak, whose shot from the right side of the box is dragged wide of the far post. Isak did score from a similar position against Ipswich last Friday, when he scored at the near post.

A minute’s silence to remember the victims of the landslides in Nepal is impeccably observed.

We are under way at Anfield. Liverpool’s Champions League campaign gets going as Andoni Iraola takes charge of his first game as a manager in this competition.

The original “This is Anfield” sign has sold at auction for almost £150,000, 10 times more than its guide price.

The sign that hung above the players’ tunnel at Liverpool’s home stadium during the 1970s had been expected to fetch between £10,000 and £15,000 after being put up for auction on Tuesday and Wednesday.

But the “talismanic” piece of football memorabilia ended up being sold by auctioneer Budds for £149,500 to a UK private buyer.

The Argentine is into the final two years of his contract, which runs out in 2028. He arrived at Liverpool in the same summer as fellow midfielders Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai, who have both signed new contracts. Mac Allister was linked with a move away from Liverpool during the summer transfer window and was candid about his contractual situation in the press conference yesterday:

“I received the news that the club was not in a position to offer me a new contract which, of course, makes me very, very sad. Everyone can see that I give my 100% for this football club every single day in training and games. Of course, I can have very good games [and] bad games, like everyone, but I always give my best.

“I see Dominik [Szoboszlai] and Ryan [Gravenberch] renewing their contracts and that makes me very happy because they deserve it. At the same time it makes me a little bit sad that I did not get mine. Of course, there is still time. The fans do not need to worry because I will give my 100% until the last day I am here. There were options to leave this summer. I think right now I am in the right club and I have the right mindset to give 100% for this club.”

Former Liverpool manager Rafa Benitez, who led the club to Champions League glory on that famous night in Istanbul in 2005, is in attendance tonight. Andoni Iraola has just shared a hug with his compatriot and perhaps Benitez will have a few words of advice for Iraola ahead of his Champions League debut as a manager.

The Dutchman has been in fine form at the start of the season for Liverpool, registering a goal and three assists in his first three games. He missed training yesterday and is not in Liverpool’s matchday squad tonight. Andoni Iraola has confirmed that Gakpo has a small adductor injury that he picked up in the Ipswich game last Friday but could be fit for the weekend against Fulham.

Atletico Madrid: Oblak; Llorente, Pubill, Romero, Hancko; Simeone, Barrios, Koke, Baena; Alvarez, Lee.Substitutes: Musso, Vargaz, Mendoza, Cardoso, Lookman, David, Grimaldo, Hjulmand, Le Normand, Dominguez, Martinez, Castillo.

When Liverpool won their sixth European Cup in 2019, they lifted it in the Wanda Metropolitano against Tottenham. This season’s Champions League final is in that very stadium and Liverpool’s Champions League campaign starts tonight against the club that plays their home games in that stadium, Atletico Madrid.

“This is going to be a challenge, I hope, all the season because it would mean we continue in all the competitions. In this case, it is not the worst scenario because we played last Friday so we have had I think a good recovery. Probably it is going to be more difficult for next weekend, especially for the next game against Tottenham in the Carabao Cup because we will have just two days, game, two days, game. But we have to get used to this; it is what big clubs do. Definitely there is part of your mind where you have to think [about] the next games. But for us, the game tomorrow is very important.”

Tonight: Atletico Madrid (home)October 14: LASK (away)October 20: Villarreal (home)November 4: Fenerbahce (away)November 25: Club Brugge (away)December 9: Porto (home)January 19: Inter Milan (away)January 27: Lens (home)

Ready for #UCL action 👊🔴 pic.twitter.com/XyOupLwsRe

Liverpool begin their Champions League campaign at home as they host Atletico Madrid at Anfield. These sides met at Anfield on matchday one last season, with Liverpool winning a dramatic game 3-2. Liverpool led 2-0 inside the opening 10 minutes before Atletico came back to level the game at 2-2. Virgil van Dijk then scored in added time to give Liverpool all three points before Atletico boss Diego Simeone was sent off for clashing with the Anfield crowd, resulting in a one-match ban.

Andoni Iraola earned his first win as Liverpool boss on Friday night as they won 2-0 away at Ipswich thanks to a quickfire early double from Alexander Isak. This will be Iraola’s first Champions League match as a manager.

“I think obviously it is a special night for me,” Iraola said. “Everyone talks [about] the Champions League nights at Anfield and also the first game is against a strong opposition, it is Atletico Madrid. [Diego] Simeone is doing an incredible job as a manager. To be all the years that he has been achieving every season the goals of the club I think is remarkable and definitely it is a big challenge for us. I think I played against him as a player, he was still a player, and I played against his teams when he was a coach and I also coached against him. So, we had a lot of precedent before. Definitely he has much more experience than me in this kind of games but I hope tomorrow we can give him a good game.

“It is one of the dreams, probably, when you start. It was difficult for me when I started my coaching career seven, eight years ago, to position myself in the position that I am right now, and I hope I can enjoy it. It is a big responsibility, massive challenge, but I feel privileged to be there in that dugout tomorrow [tonight] and now my thinking is about putting the team together in a position where we can play a good game, win the game and start strong in this Champions League.”

Atletico Madrid currently sit sixth in La Liga and suffered their first defeat on Saturday as they lost 3-0 at Athletic Bilbao. They did reach the semi-finals of the Champions League last season, where they fell to Arsenal 2-1 on aggregate.

“We are coming into a marvellous stadium and there will be a great atmosphere,” Simeone said. “We will have to look good from the start of the game because it will be full on. He [Andoni Iraola] works very well with the team, focusing on the tactical awareness of each player. It takes time to find the right path, but he is growing and improving and he has some very good players.”

#1813. AC Milan 3-1 Inter: Moreira inspires commanding fourth straight derby win

AC Milan recorded a huge win in the derby against Inter, scoring three times in the first half to secure a 3-1 win.

It did not take long for Milan to go in front, with Christian Pulisic heading in a cross from Diego Moreira. Then, just a few minutes later, Adrien Rabiot was on hand to fire in a corner first time and make it a two-goal lead.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Alessandro Bastoni scored from a corner to make it a one-goal lead once again, but then Moreira’s free-kick re-established the two-goal lead and that would be enough to see the Rossoneri through to the end of the game.

It marked a fourth straight win for Milan in the derby and it reduces the gap to the city rivals back down to four points.

Ruben Amorim chose to make six changes from the team that lost to Bologna on Wednesday night, with Mario Gila, Sankhoun Diawara, Luka Modric, Adrien Rabiot, Diego Moreira and Christian Pulisic all getting the nod.

Inside four minutes, Milan took the lead and it was the derby talisman Christian Pulisic who struck once again. It was quite a simple move down the right side in the end, with Diego Moreira checking back inside onto his left foot and whipped in a simply perfect cross for Pulisic to nod in from a few yards out.

Then, just a few minutes later, Milan doubled their advantage from a set-piece after another good spell of pressure. A low delivery from Moreira found the run of Rabiot towards the near post, who somehow managed to divert it in via the far post to make it 2-0.

Midway through the first half, Inter got themselves back into the game through a dead ball of their own. A corner was flicked on at the near post towards Bastoni, who was on hand to nod in from a few yards with the Milan defenders rooted.

Inter assumed the ascendancy after the goal, and they twice threatened in quick succession shortly after their first goal. Calhanoglu had a shot tipped over from the edge of the box, then another flicked header from a corner drew a desperate reaction save from Maignan.

Milan continued to give their city rivals opportunities to try and make it a brand new game. A silly foul by Pavlovic on Spence drew a free-kick just off the right edge of the box, though the eventual shot from Diouf was grasped by Maignan.

Just over 10 minutes before the break, Inter had another chance to draw themselves level. A cross from the left was not cut out by Koni De Winter, and the ball fells to Spence who fired with his left foot, but the Frenchman makes a brilliant reaction save to deflect the shot out for a corner.

Just two minutes before the break, Milan restored their two-goal advantage thanks to a quite simply beautiful free-kick from Diego Moreira. After getting two assists to his name already on the night, he turned scorer with a fantastic attempt that was up and over the wall, dipping just enough to land inside the near right post.

Ten minutes into the second half, Inter had the first big opening and it fell to their recent danger man Carlos Augusto. A cross to the far post wasn’t tracked by anyone and the wing-back ghosted in at the far post, heading it wide from about a yard off the ground.

With 25 minutes left, a corner this time for Milan: Modric’s cross from the left finds Rabiot at the near post, who tries to head it in, but his connection was poor and the ball went straight out.

In the 75th minute, it looked like the game was going to be on once again when the referee gave a penalty for what he adjudged to be a handball on Mario Gila. The replays show that the cross struck his midriff, and therefore the penalty was overturned to be a corner.

With the game settled into a rhythm of attack versus defence, Amorim chose to make a double change with eight minutes to go. Pulisic and Diawara were the ones who came off, with Alphadjo Cisse and Davide Bartesaghi the ones to come on.

In the penultimate minute of added time, a double sub came from Amorim. Ramos and Moreira came off, Filippo Terracciano and Omari Hutchinson came on.

Alphadjo Cisse came on inside the final minutes and immediately came close to scoring. The Italian forward tried a curling shot from outside the area, but Martinez saved well to put it out for a corner, keeping it 3-1.

#1812. Barcelona vs. Aston Villa: Head-to-head record and past meetings before Champions League battle

By Ben Knapton | 01 Nov 2026 11:24

Two of the fiercest attacking forces the Champions League has to offer collide at Camp Nou on Tuesday, when Barcelona and Aston Villa meet on matchday four of the 2026-27 league phase.

La Blaugrana have some continental wrongs to right after losing 4-2 to holders Paris Saint-Germain on matchday three, a result that ended their perfect start to the current tournament.

On the other hand, Aston Villa are seeking a fourth win from four matches in the UCL, having already bested Club Brugge, Fenerbahce and Viking FK while scoring 12 goals along the way.

Here, Sports Mole takes an in-depth look at the head-to-head record and previous meetings between the two sides.

Barcelona and Aston Villa never met in the 21st century before the 2026-27 Champions League, which will also mark their first head-to-head in the top tier of European football.

However, the two former continental champions did lock horns four times in the 20th century, and Barcelona came out on top in two of those clashes, while losing one and playing out one draw.

That solitary stalemate came in the two teams' inaugural meeting in the 1977-78 UEFA Cup quarter-finals, as Villa pulled off an astonishing comeback from 2-0 down to draw 2-2 in the first leg at Villa Park.

Johan Cruyff put Barcelona ahead in the 20th minute before Rafael Zuviria's 80th-minute effort, but Ken McNaught's 87th-minute response and John Deehan's 89th-minute equaliser rescued an unlikely draw for the Lions.

Barca were not to be denied, though, as Rinus Michels's men triumphed 2-1 in the second leg at Camp Nou two weeks later, fighting back from 1-0 down to prevail before losing to PSV Eindhoven in the semi-finals.

Villa and Barcelona would reunite five years later in the 1982 UEFA Super Cup - contested over two legs in January 1983 - the Lions entering as European Cup holders and the Blaugrana as European Cup Winners' Cup champions.

The first leg - held at Camp Nou - ended 1-0 in favour of Barcelona, but Aston Villa turned the tide in chaotic circumstances in the second leg at Villa Park, winning 3-0 after extra time for a 3-1 aggregate triumph.

The second leg ended 10v9, as Villa received one red card and Barcelona two, but the Lions ultimately clinched their last European trophy for 44 years before Unai Emery masterminded their run to Europa League glory in 2025-26.

Jan 26, 1983: Aston Villa 3-0 Barcelona (Super Cup)

Jan 19, 1983: Barcelona 1-0 Aston Villa (Super Cup)

Mar 15, 1978: Barcelona 2-1 Aston Villa (UEFA Cup)

Mar 01, 1978: Aston Villa 2-2 Barcelona (UEFA Cup)

#1811. Harry Kane makes admission after Ballon d'Or nightmare

By Naim Beneddra | 01 Nov 2026 11:42

Harry Kane has admitted that he could have played for another hour without scoring after enduring a frustrating first appearance since winning the 2026 Ballon d'Or.

The England captain missed a penalty and failed to register a single shot on target as Bayern Munich were held to a dramatic 2-2 draw by Borussia Dortmund at the Allianz Arena on Saturday evening.

It was an unexpected outcome to a remarkable week for the 33-year-old, who had been presented with football's most prestigious individual award in London on Monday, becoming the first English winner since Michael Owen in 2001.

Kane received a special tribute from Bayern before kick-off, entering the pitch separately from his teammates and displaying the trophy alongside his family in front of 75,000 supporters.

However, the celebrations gave way to an unusually difficult evening in front of goal, prompting the former Tottenham Hotspur striker to deliver a candid assessment of his performance.

Already a club legend! ❤️? Harry Kane with a few words to the fans ?❤ https://t.co/K85U3spcz4

Speaking to reporters after the Klassiker, Kane acknowledged that he had fallen below his usual standards, although he was equally disappointed with Bayern's collective display.

"Today probably wasn't my best performance or the team's best performance, but that's just life," the England international said, as quoted by AFP.

"That's just part of being a striker, a footballer.

"I probably could have been out there for another hour today and the ball wouldn't have gone in the back of the net."

Kane's frustration was understandable given the opportunities he had to add another goal to his impressive tally.

With Bayern leading 1-0 early in the second half, he stepped up to take a penalty after Felix Nmecha was penalised for handball.

The striker struck his effort against the crossbar, squandering a chance to double the hosts' advantage.

According to Opta, it was only the second penalty Kane had failed to convert in 27 Bundesliga attempts, with his previous miss coming against Wolfsburg in May.

His difficulties continued when a misplaced pass was intercepted by Nico Schlotterbeck during the move that ended with Serhou Guirassy bringing Dortmund level.

Kane subsequently struck the woodwork again, although that effort would not have counted because of an offside decision.

Perhaps the most revealing statistic was his overall shooting record: six attempts, none of which hit the target.

Opta noted that only one player had registered more shots without testing the goalkeeper in a Bundesliga game this season.

Yet Kane still made an important contribution, heading Joshua Kimmich's cross back across goal for Dayot Upamecano to restore Bayern's lead.

That assist took his tally to 10 direct goal involvements in eight league appearances this season, comprising four goals and six assists.

The figures provide some perspective on an evening that was disappointing by the standards of the newly crowned Ballon d'Or winner, rather than evidence of a prolonged loss of form.

Kane, who scored 73 goals for club and country last season, was reluctant to dwell on the setback.

"You have to take it on the chin sometimes. It was an incredible week, but the focus for sure now is on the games ahead," he added.

Kane's determination to move forward comes at an important moment for Bayern, whose demanding fixture schedule has been complicated by fresh injury concerns.

Ismael Saibari, Serge Gnabry and Michael Olise were all forced off during Saturday's draw, leaving the German champions facing uncertainty over several attacking options.

Those setbacks add to the absences of Jamal Musiala and Luis Diaz, potentially increasing Bayern's dependence on their leading striker.

The club are also temporarily without head coach Vincent Kompany on the touchline as he continues his recovery from a health problem, with assistant Aaron Danks overseeing the team against Dortmund.

Bayern face another significant examination on Tuesday, November 3, when they travel to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League.

Kane has already indicated that he expects to be available for the encounter, while stressing that the squad will need to cope with a demanding run of fixtures.

"For Atletico, I'll be ready to go. It's an important game for us," he told Bulinews.

"We're going to a really tough place away from home so we're going to need everyone to step up."

Bayern remain unbeaten in the Bundesliga after eight matches, although Dortmund's late equaliser ensured that the title rivals stayed level on 18 points, with the Bavarians ahead on goal difference.

For Kane, the immediate challenge is to rediscover the finishing touch that helped him claim the Ballon d'Or.

His performance against Dortmund was a reminder that even Europe's most prolific forwards can experience difficult afternoons, but the England captain will have an early opportunity to respond in Madrid.
